A +19.4pp gap on the Argentina side. Argentina v Austria in FIFA World Cup 2026 is the match. The model has Argentina stronger than the market does — that's the reason this fires as a Pick rather than a Pass.

Public Elo rates Argentina 310 points higher than the other side (Argentina 2140, Austria 1830). The match model's logistic translates that Elo gap directly into a win-probability. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Argentina to win at 76%, the draw at 11%, and Austria to win at 13%. The Desk's three-way distribution is calibrated against the W/D/L resolution Polymarket and Kalshi settle on, not against the exact scoreline. Argentina sits at 76% of the mass.

On the same three-way, Kalshi: Argentina to win at 56%, the draw at 24%, and Austria to win at 16%. Kalshi has Argentina at 56%, which prices out at American odds of −130; the model has the same side at 76%. The +19.4pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On Argentina, that haircut lands the model at 66%; the market is at 56%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +9.8pp. The Desk's posture is that calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures — we're not claiming the market is generally wrong, only that this side, on this fixture, looks mispriced. Selection is the dimension this verdict adds value on.

The number above is the most recent read; it isn't frozen. With kickoff roughly 32 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. Injury news, the actual XI, and weather conditions at kickoff all feed back into the prior when they land. We republish on every refresh. The Desk surfaces edge; what to do with that surface is a reader's call.
